prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” attorney for every car-accident case — the right lawyer depends on the specifics of your crash, injuries, and goals. I can help you find a great fit. First, here’s how to identify top personal-injury counsel in Chicago and what to do next.

How to choose the right attorney
- Look for trial experience and a strong track record in car-accident cases (settlements and verdicts, especially for injuries like yours).  
- Check credentials: Illinois bar standing, board certification if any, peer-review ratings (Martindale-Hubbell), Super Lawyers, Avvo.  
- Prefer contingency-fee arrangements (no upfront fee; lawyer is paid from recovery) so you pay only if they win.  
- Ask whether the lawyer handles cases like yours regularly (severe injury, wrongful death, catastrophic, uninsured motorist, hit-and-run, commercial vehicle).  
- Confirm the lawyer will try the case if needed — many insurers settle only when faced with a credible trial lawyer.  
- Communication: who will handle day-to-day contact? How often will you get updates?  
- Local knowledge: experience with Chicago courts, Cook County judges, and local medical providers/liens is helpful.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?  
- Have you handled cases with injuries like mine? Outcomes?  
- Who in the firm will work on my case? Contact frequency?  
- What is your fee structure and expense policy? (Contingency %, who advances costs?)  
- What is an estimated range of value for my case and why?  
- Any potential conflicts of interest?  

Immediate steps you should take now
- Get medical attention and follow doctor instructions (medical records are key).  
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicle damage, injuries, road conditions, traffic signals, and clothing; save repair estimates and medical bills.  
- Get the police report number and officer name.  
- Collect witness names/contacts if possible.  
- Don’t give recorded statements to the insurer or sign releases without an attorney.  
- Note: Illinois generally has a two-year statute of limitations for personal-injury suits — act promptly.

Where to search for reputable Chicago attorneys
- Illinois State Bar Association and Chicago Bar Association directories.  
- Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, and Avvo for ratings and reviews.  
- Local law-firm websites (look for case results and attorney bios).  
- Personal referrals from friends/family or other lawyers.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list of well-regarded Chicago personal-injury attorneys tailored to your zip code and the severity/type of injury, or  
- Draft an email/phone script and a checklist for your initial consultations.

Tell me your zip code and a brief summary of the crash/injuries (minor/moderate/serious, who’s at fault, any police report), and I’ll pull together a targeted list and next steps.
